## Scope, progress and next action

Chronic pancreatitis, pancreatic insufficiency, neoplastic cysts, pancreatic adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumors and pancreatic resection complications. Acute pancreatitis and inflammatory collections belong to pancreas-acute-pancreatitis. General endocrine syndromes belong to adrenal-men-endocrine.

Owner direction is increased difficult, useful coverage and improved existing items. The clinic has no ICU/ED/trauma bay. New hospital-level work is already implemented as review of outside records in clinic; no new clinical setting is proposed. Educational tier, clinic acuity, historical acuity, capability and progression gate are recorded separately.

**Counts:** audited 17; kept 5; rewritten 2; retired-and-replaced proposed 10; new 18. The sidecar has 20 questions / 20 scored concepts in 11 cases, including eight multi-part cases. Two existing concepts are reused and eighteen new identities are proposed. Three changed-meaning links point to previous constructs without moving their histories.

17 unique exact assigned variant/inventory rows: 16 materialized and one source-only; 28 distinct captured visible case/node contexts. Proposed supply is two rewrites on unchanged stable concepts plus eighteen new questions/new identities. Several old variants consolidate into one draft; replacements are not counted twice.

The five clinically approved variants are kept exactly, with their current quality limits recorded. No independent PASS was present for an assigned variant. The old N2 v3 editorial park remains. Assigned unkeyed slots: 0; assigned withheld points: 0. Three additional unscored policy boundaries below are withheld. No ship manifest, registry, runtime, old question or shared planning file was edited.

Next action: Manager inspects actual five-file changes, routes the out-of-lane trauma-thoracic type errors to their owner, obtains independent item/composition review, resolves listed clinical questions and decides exact acceptance/integration.


## Ranked testable concepts and coverage/gap matrix

Ranks are qualitative judgments of testability and practical consequences, not official exam weights or observed performance. Duct/venous anatomy, cyst pathology and sampling, exocrine physiology, diagnosis, staging, interventions, complications and follow-up were considered. Embryologic duct variants and acute inflammatory-collection treatment belong to the acute topic; hormonal diagnosis and general MEN care remain with the endocrine lane.

### 1. IPMN high-risk findings and action

Decision: Use ductal and mural findings to escalate a cyst to pancreatic surgical evaluation rather than routine surveillance.

Raw evidence: Enhancing nodule 7 mm and main duct 11 mm, with surgical fitness documented.

Credible error: Use a negative or scant fluid sample to justify routine surveillance. Consequence: Delay evaluation of potentially advanced neoplasia.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: Existing coverage repeats a compatible cyst label, not a management-changing risk decision.

Existing concepts: concept.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recognition. Assigned variants: question.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recognition.v2, question.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recognition.v1, question.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recognition.v3, question.pancreatic-cyst.mcn-pattern-recognition.v4.

Proposed questions: question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.ipmn-high-risk-plan.v1.

Atomic support: claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.ipmn-high-risk, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.cyst-imaging-limits, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.cyst-eus-uncertainty. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.acg-cysts-2018, source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.sirm-aisp-cysts-2026, source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.kyoto-ipmn-2024.

### 2. Pancreatic cancer vessel anatomy and sequence

Decision: Use potentially reconstructible venous involvement to select neoadjuvant planning without abandoning curative intent.

Raw evidence: Venous narrowing/contour change with patent segments, no major arterial contact and no distant disease.

Credible error: Operate immediately because reconstruction appears technically possible. Consequence: Select an unfavorable immediate operation or prematurely abandon curative-intent reassessment.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: Approved tail-operation variants do not test systemic-first sequencing or reconstructible venous involvement.

Existing concepts: concept.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.distal-pancreatectomy-with-splenectomy. Assigned variants: question.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.clinic-counseling.v1, question.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.operative-candidate.v1, question.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.referral-plan.v1, question.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.spleen-counseling.v1, question.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.procedure-by-location.v1.

Proposed questions: question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.borderline-systemic-first.v1.

Atomic support: claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.cancer-neoadjuvant, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.cancer-reconstructible-vein, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.cancer-metastatic-boundary. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.pancreatic-cancer-consensus-2020, source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.nci-pancreas-2025.

### 3. Distant staging before a pancreatic operation

Decision: Resolve a management-changing hepatic lesion before declaring pancreatic disease localized. Change treatment intent when representative distant tissue confirms pancreatic cancer spread.

Raw evidence: The hepatic focus is uncharacterized on existing CT and has no prior comparison. Targeted liver core is concordant metastatic adenocarcinoma; multiple hepatic lesions are present.

Credible error: Proceed using favorable pancreatic vascular anatomy as complete staging. Apply the memorized tail-operation rule despite newly proven multifocal distant disease. Consequence: Plan a nonbeneficial major operation or falsely deny surgery based on an uncertain focus. Offer a major nonstandard operation without first addressing disseminated disease.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: No current decision addresses indeterminate distant lesions or intent change after representative tissue.

Existing concepts: concept.pancreatic-tail-adenocarcinoma.distal-pancreatectomy-with-splenectomy. ### 4. Cyst characterization and correct referral target

Decision: Choose the next study to characterize an incidentally detected cyst whose duct relationship is unresolved. Identify the older cyst as distinct from a new inflammatory collection and choose the appropriate remaining characterization study.

Raw evidence: Only thick-section CT urogram images exist; no suspicious mural focus or adequate pancreatic characterization is supplied. A exists on the pre-attack study; the current dedicated CT still leaves duct relation unresolved.

Credible error: Choose EUS immediately because every unknown pancreatic cyst seems to require fluid. Attribute the pre-existing A to the admission that produced B. Consequence: Premature invasive testing or repeated nondiagnostic imaging. Puncture or treat the wrong disease pathway.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: Four repetitive live MRCP variants and retained N2 chronology drafts; consolidate and strengthen true competitors.

Existing concepts: concept.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessment, concept.n2.pancreatic-cyst-predates-pancreatitis, concept.n2r3.pancreatic-referral-target-characterization. Assigned variants: question.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessment.v2, question.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessment.v1, question.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessment.v3, question.pancreatic-cyst.mrcp-duct-assessment.v4, question.n2.pancreatic-cyst-predates-pancreatitis.v1, question.n2.pancreatic-cyst-predates-pancreatitis.v2, question.n2.pancreatic-cyst-predates-pancreatitis.v3.

### 5. Postoperative infection and effective source control

Decision: Investigate secondary causes of postoperative vomiting when inflammation and drain findings suggest an abdominal complication. Choose the least invasive effective source-control route for an accessible postoperative collection in a stable patient.

Raw evidence: New inflammation together with abrupt decrease of previously enzyme-rich drainage. Drain tip outside an accessible rim-enhancing collection, with ongoing fever but stable circulation.

Credible error: Order gastric-emptying testing for a familiar postoperative symptom pattern. Choose ERCP because the fluid is pancreatic, leaving the infected cavity undrained. Consequence: Delay recognition and treatment of a postoperative collection. Persistent infection or unnecessary reoperation.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: The retained mapping variant does not establish supported modality ranking or score cavity source control.

Existing concepts: concept.n1r3.postoperative-pancreatic-source-mapping. Assigned variants: question.n1.postoperative-ascites-ct.v3.

Proposed questions: question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-vomiting-inflammation.v1, question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-infected-collection-drain.v1.

Atomic support: claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-secondary-emptying, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-infected-collection, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-stepup, claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.chronic-internal-fistula-stent. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.jsg-chronic-2022, source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postoperative-complications-2026.

### 6. Postpancreatectomy warning bleeding

Decision: Recognize a transient postoperative bleeding episode as a vascular warning rather than wait for recurrence.

Raw evidence: New fresh drain blood and hemoglobin fall after pancreatic leakage, without a luminal bleeding presentation.

Credible error: Defer vascular evaluation because visible bleeding stopped. Consequence: Miss a warning preceding major postoperative hemorrhage.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: No assigned variant; consequential warning-event and bleeding-compartment gap.

Existing concepts: None. Assigned variants: None.

Proposed questions: question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-transient-drain-bleed.v1.

Atomic support: claim.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-sentinel-bleed. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postoperative-complications-2026.

### 7. Chronic insufficiency versus persistent obstructive pain

Decision: Correct enzyme-food mismatch before labeling pancreatic enzyme therapy ineffective. Select duct-directed surgery when endoscopic decompression has failed to provide sustained pain relief.

Raw evidence: All capsules are taken at bedtime, separate from daytime meals/snacks. Repeated temporary response plus a still-dilated duct; no dominant head mass.

Credible error: Escalate the dose because weight loss implies treatment failure. Repeat stenting indefinitely because it produced a brief response. Consequence: Persistent malabsorption despite unnecessary prescription escalation. Delay a more durable duct-directed option while disability continues.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: No assigned chronic-disease intervention question.

Existing concepts: None. Assigned variants: None.

### 8. A new mass in chronic pancreatitis and sample adequacy

Decision: Recognize that a negative off-target sample does not resolve a suspicious new pancreatic lesion.

Raw evidence: Needle tip beside the lesion; the submitted specimen lacks representative lesional tissue.

Credible error: Accept fibrosis as proof that the mass is chronic inflammatory disease. Consequence: Miss a treatable cancer or start inappropriate systemic therapy.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: No question distinguishes adjacent fibrosis from a representative negative sample.

Existing concepts: None. Assigned variants: None.

### 9. Large symptomatic presumed MCN and fluid-test limits

Decision: Integrate a presumed mucinous cyst's burden and symptoms without treating CEA or scant cytology as a cancer test.

Raw evidence: The large older lesion compresses the stomach after B resolves; the cytology is scant.

Credible error: Choose surveillance because no high-grade cells were identified. Consequence: Mismanage a symptomatic neoplastic cyst as benign fluid or postpone indicated surgical evaluation.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

### 10. Nonfunctioning NET: surveillance and later progression

Decision: Balance a small nonfunctioning NET's behavior against pancreatic intervention rather than operate on every NET label. Reassess a prior low-risk NET when growth and duct proximity change operative needs.

Raw evidence: 8-mm nonfunctioning grade-1 tumor, unchanged duct, no spread and available follow-up. 2.8-cm deep body lesion only 1 mm from the main duct with new upstream dilation.

Credible error: Choose enucleation simply because the lesion is small and localized. Enucleate to preserve pancreas using the original low-grade label. Consequence: Expose a selected low-risk patient to avoidable pancreatic surgery. Duct injury or an inadequate operative strategy, or delayed treatment if surveillance persists.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

Existing coverage: No assigned NET question.

Existing concepts: None. Assigned variants: None.

### 11. Functional NET: local planning and operation extent

Decision: Choose additional lesion/duct assessment when it changes surgery for a localized functional NET. Apply lesion behavior and duct separation to a limited operation for a localized insulinoma.

Raw evidence: Localized focus already seen on adequate CT, but main-duct separation unresolved. Solitary superficial 12-mm functional lesion, 6-mm duct separation, no invasion or suspicious nodes.

Credible error: Choose receptor PET because it sounds most specific for a NET. Choose central pancreatectomy because the lesion lies in the neck, without using its superficial position and duct clearance. Consequence: Plan an inappropriate pancreatic operation or add a noncontributory study. Unnecessary major resection or, with different anatomy, duct injury from an unsuitable limited procedure.

Relevance: High qualitative editorial relevance: practical general-surgery decisions and credible resident errors. No claimed ABSITE frequency, official blueprint percentage or measured difficulty. Changes investigation, treatment intent, intervention extent or follow-up.

### Remaining research scope

- **Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm and rare cystic NETs:** Potentially testable operation/referral decisions; lower editorial priority than the consequential gaps drafted here. Next action: Later bounded case with credible operative competitors; avoid another morphology-label item. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.sirm-aisp-cysts-2026.
- **Autoimmune pancreatitis and hereditary cancer surveillance:** Important differential/risk pathways. No invented steroid trial, IgG4 cutoff or surveillance interval. Next action: Verify current disease-specific primary guidance. General endocrine syndromes remain adrenal-men-endocrine owned. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.pancreatic-cancer-consensus-2020.
- **Technical anatomy, chyle leak and postresection endocrine care:** Duct/venous/resection anatomy is represented; pancreas divisum and acute collections belong to the acute topic. Exact chyle/drain prophylaxis policies are not scored. Next action: Add a consequential technical/complication decision only with direct exact support, without protected operative figures or a new inpatient setting. Sources: source.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postoperative-complications-2026.

### Excluded or limited source candidates

- **European cyst guideline 2018, Gut; doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2018-316027:** Publisher page returned 403; article has CC BY-NC 4.0 and BMJ reserves other AI/TDM uses. Excluded from new claim support because downstream noncommercial scope and access terms are not assumed. Historical surveillance disagreement is visible but unscored. No supported claim IDs.
- **AGA 2023 exocrine pancreatic insufficiency guidance:** 403 on full guidance and public summary pages. No search-snippet dose or watery-stool cutoff adopted; NIDDK and JSG support the authored drug-food timing decision. No supported claim IDs.
- **HaPanEU chronic pancreatitis 2017, SAGE:** Not ingested or used for a new claim; publisher AI/reuse concerns avoided with verified JSG and current CC BY surgical review. No supported claim IDs.
- **ISGPS 2016 update and noncommercial/no-derivatives postoperative reviews:** No grading threshold or new key derived from inaccessible/nonreusable snippets. Current CC BY 2026 review supports the authored complication chain, with a single-publication limitation. No supported claim IDs.

### Unkeyed withheld policies (not scored-question verdict totals)

- **withheld.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.stop-low-risk-ipmn-surveillance** ? Continue MRI surveillance versus Stop surveillance in selected stable small cysts. Kyoto 2024 permits conditional stopping in selected patients; European 2018 favors follow-up while fit, and SIRM-AISP 2026 describes continuing uncertainty. Do not average intervals or impose a universal five-year stop rule. Next action: Melissa/manager decide a patient-specific policy after current independent guideline verification. Question and concept IDs remain null.
- **withheld.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.one-to-two-cm-nfnet** ? Structured surveillance versus Enucleation versus Formal pancreatic resection. NANETS individualizes asymptomatic 1-2 cm tumors. Size alone does not establish one universal key. Drafts use selected subcentimeter or clearly larger progressing lesions. Next action: Obtain exact risk, grade, duct anatomy and a named clinical decision before authoring. Question and concept IDs remain null.
- **withheld.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.chronic-head-operation-ranking** ? Frey procedure versus Beger/other duodenum-preserving resection versus Pancreaticoduodenectomy. Permitted surgical review describes broadly comparable long-term outcomes. Morphology, cancer suspicion and expertise matter. No universal operation superiority inferred. Next action: Build a narrowly constrained later case with a clinician or score the strategy class without ranking equivalent operations. Question and concept IDs remain null.

#### prior-cyst-target - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.prior-cyst-target.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.prior-cyst-target.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `35e2aa02c88a1e85871aa487832eba6792839deb59a22fc7a22d9101ea4b4bbc`.

- **clarity:** Task and all options now dispose of the same named procedural referral: characterize A, drain A transgastrically, or drain A percutaneously.
- **cues:** Removed the unresolved-duct phrase and duplicate CT foil. Both lesions retain their actual dated sizes and the patient retains symptoms.
- **fairness:** The old MRI-over-EUS ranking is withdrawn. The scored construct is target/chronology characterization, consistent with the stable referral-target concept. EUS is a reasonable characterization route for the enlarged symptomatic cyst, and MRI is not scored as inferior.
- **suggestions:** Chronology must first distinguish A from B, then change the proposed procedure. Node-two results remain subsequent studies, regardless of the characterization sequence.
- **outcome:** Fair moderate version; no remaining forced MRI/EUS ordering or task/option mismatch is asserted.

#### mcn-large-symptomatic - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.mcn-large-symptomatic.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.mcn-large-symptomatic.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `d4a123461df886545e95c27405ae772ee4b04bdfe346c016e8c6c1b2992c552f`.

- **clarity:** Complete management task and the updated results identify A consistently after B resolves.
- **cues:** Replaced already-dismissed cystgastrostomy with repeat EUS sampling. Removed the causal phrase assigning fullness directly to the indentation.
- **fairness:** Gastric indentation with intact mucosa, ongoing meal-related fullness and resolution of B are observations to interpret. High CEA and scant bland cytology remain competing evidence without being used as cancer tests.
- **suggestions:** The nearest competitor is obtaining more tissue before surgery. Feedback states why the size/symptom referral does not require a malignant aspirate, and the rubric gives the smaller/asymptomatic surveillance counterfactual.
- **outcome:** Two-step moderate-hard candidate, pending independent and exact clinical review.

#### pert-administration - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.pert-administration.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.pert-administration.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `6156b3104acea685ba83d4d8d000afa15de40a23770b218284479ae78fe4e7d4`.

- **clarity:** Prescription, meal log and actual preparation are distinguished. Task asks for the first management change rather than presuming the written prescription is wrong.
- **cues:** Removed bedtime dosing and options that merely repeat that error. Food timing and prescribed amounts are correct; the preparation demonstration must be interpreted.
- **fairness:** Product-specific regulatory labeling supports intact granules in acidic soft food when capsules cannot be swallowed. No numerical dose, dose adequacy claim or guaranteed symptom response is invented. Dose reassessment and acid suppression remain credible later alternatives.
- **suggestions:** The changed objective is preservation of enteric delivery, not food synchronization. A new concept identity links to the old one without moving FSRS history.
- **outcome:** Fair moderate new-meaning version; medication mechanism is scored without adding arithmetic.

#### mass-nondiagnostic-sample - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.mass-nondiagnostic-sample.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.mass-nondiagnostic-sample.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `a3abab1791ab0da4dc0528b7b65a49860578c9ddc139039e936dcfd94cff9e7b`.

- **clarity:** The table labels the new CT target, sampled EUS site and actual specimen, while retaining the systemic-treatment constraint.
- **cues:** Removed the explicit missed-target interpretation and long key-only explanation. Every option names a concrete tissue-acquisition route and target.
- **fairness:** EUS core and CT-guided core sample the same pancreatic primary; ERCP brushings target the actual distal stricture. The negative neck specimen is not presented as evidence that representative EUS has failed.
- **suggestions:** Learner must assess specimen relevance and then choose a representative preferred route. No biopsy-before-every-operation rule or invented threshold is taught.
- **outcome:** Two-step moderate-hard candidate; all offered strategies are clinically plausible tissue routes.

        "phrase": "the needle images place its tip beside the CT lesion",
        "why": "The stem directly reveals the procedural miss; it need not be inferred from the specimen and imaging relationship."
      },
      {
        "phrase": "Repeat EUS-guided core sampling of the head lesion",
        "why": "This is the uniquely explicit repair of the named missed target and is longer and more specific than the other investigations."
      },
      {
        "phrase": "before systemic treatment is selected",
        "why": "Together with the stated plan to treat only if cancer is confirmed, the task further channels the learner toward tissue acquisition. This is a legitimate care-stage constraint but largely supplies the intended second step."
      }
    ],
    "fairness": [
      "Representative tissue is needed before selecting systemic anticancer treatment, and a sample beside a suspicious lesion cannot exclude cancer within it. Repeat targeted EUS sampling is the best offered investigation; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified.",
      "ERCP brush cytology can provide diagnostic information, but the text does not present a biliary target or other reason to prefer it to re-sampling the solid pancreatic lesion. MRI cannot replace the tissue requirement in this stated treatment pathway.",
      "The item is clear and high yield, but target miss followed by target re-sampling is essentially a direct repair, not two substantial inferences."
    ],
    "suggestions": [
      "Preserve the sampling limitation, but express it through a concise specimen/target record and make representative tissue acquisition compete with another genuinely plausible next diagnostic strategy.",
      "Keep the treatment-stage constraint for fairness; obtain the added difficulty from interpreting evidence adequacy, not from hiding the need for tissue or adding unsupported thresholds."
    ]

#### borderline-systemic-first - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.borderline-systemic-first.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.borderline-systemic-first.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `ac6fad85e8998ae0bce42b1c6608d0189786fd38377e2201347ef7af955c9ab1`.

- **clarity:** Initial treatment intent and sequence are explicit for all three plans.
- **cues:** Removed no-resection-reassessment punitive wording. Reassessment is not reserved as a key-only sign of a careful plan.
- **fairness:** The venous findings support a potentially reconstructable borderline interpretation but do not guarantee reconstruction. Named clinical confirmation of exact anatomic classification remains required, as for all new clinical drafts.
- **suggestions:** No unsupported contact-degree cutoff added. Deciding observations and the clearly-resectable counterfactual distinguish the competing surgical sequence.
- **outcome:** Two-step moderate-hard candidate with a specific clinical-signoff question, not a new unkeyed design proposal.

#### neoadjuvant-jaundice-drainage - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.neoadjuvant-jaundice-drainage.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.neoadjuvant-jaundice-drainage.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `538bdcbf264855d77b830859781165eabcf99e712d536b7810f5004ad1804cc6`.

- **clarity:** Task asks for a pre-treatment management plan rather than directing that drainage occur.
- **cues:** Removed explicit papilla-access permission and surgical bypass. Choices compare metal drainage, plastic drainage and treatment before drainage.
- **fairness:** Obstruction, multi-cycle horizon and unaltered anatomy are supplied. No bilirubin cutoff or universal covered-versus-uncovered metal claim is introduced. A CC BY comparative review independently supports recurrent-obstruction and reintervention differences.
- **suggestions:** Feedback explains clinical durability rather than invoking a verified-consensus authority label. The rubric requires recognition of obstruction before stent selection.
- **outcome:** Fair moderate two-stage preparation decision; exact metal design is not scored.

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.indeterminate-liver-staging.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.indeterminate-liver-staging.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `4fd8143df05951e4c6c5722115e5e725ea5717892991a5973857845cae9a79b1`.

- **clarity:** The immediate task is initial characterization of a specific hepatic staging focus, not whole-body staging by any possible method.
- **cues:** All options address the same liver finding. Removed regional-node EUS and unchanged repeat CT; MRI is no longer the sole liver-targeted option.
- **fairness:** Actual acquisition, 7-mm size and nonvisualization on targeted ultrasound support characterizing the focus before attempting tissue. MRI is preferred for this purpose; PET and biopsy retain stated subsequent or complementary roles without fabricated performance cutoffs.
- **suggestions:** Learner first separates favorable local anatomy from unresolved distant staging, then selects a characterization study. No metastatic label is inferred from CT alone.
- **outcome:** Fair moderate version with credible same-target alternatives rather than a claimed hard sensitivity contest.

#### confirmed-liver-disease-intent - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.confirmed-liver-disease-intent.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.confirmed-liver-disease-intent.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `827a22cbd2b1318c14c16d5c54ed9aaeb05a9a9785525d7cfb7c6d41a5feab99`.

- **clarity:** Removed all authoring-system, version-history and concept-transfer language from resident feedback.
- **cues:** The update gives tissue location and matching malignant-gland morphology instead of announcing the metastatic diagnosis. The key does not repeat that removed label.
- **fairness:** The positive hepatic specimen is not obscured or made equivocal. It must be interpreted as distant tumor, then translated into initial treatment intent. Three parallel treatment pathways distinguish initial disease control from routine preoperative sequencing.
- **suggestions:** No new peritoneal-cytology or immunostain staging rule was adopted. The standard metastatic boundary uses the existing consensus and government sources; exceptional later local therapy is not categorically forbidden.

- **clarity:** Replaced unchanged duct with no focal narrowing or upstream dilation, consistent with feedback.
- **cues:** Removed follow-up permission and supplied grade label. Sampled Ki-67 is shown as an observation, with no exact grade cutoff added.
- **fairness:** The learner integrates low sampled proliferation, subcentimeter size, absent hormone syndrome and actual duct findings. Sampling limits remain explicit; surveillance is acceptable rather than compulsory. No 1-2 cm policy rule is scored.
- **suggestions:** Retained a fair moderate risk-and-management version. The decision-changing functional-syndrome counterfactual and credible enucleation error are explicit; it is not represented as a difficult grading exercise.
- **outcome:** Fair moderate candidate; every original duct/feedback mismatch is resolved.

#### functional-net-anatomic-study - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.functional-net-anatomic-study.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.functional-net-anatomic-study.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `0c546b6fb93598fbddef796a83d5d7575e8c732c99f1f60284279ad8cff457be`.

- **clarity:** The remaining operative question is functional assignment among two identified NETs, not a supplied missing duct measurement.
- **cues:** Removed named duct-distance gap and access/availability permission. CT/MRI/EUS report two anatomic candidates without assigning secretion.
- **fairness:** Known MEN1 and biochemically established insulin excess are supplied rather than tested in the endocrine topic. Calcium stimulation can add functional regionalization; it is not promised to name a unique tumor or outrank every tracer. No complete exclusion of metastasis is claimed.
- **suggestions:** The new concept and fictional patient distinguish this objective from EUS operative-anatomy mapping. Conventional biopsy and receptor imaging are credible tests but do not by themselves assign insulin production.
- **outcome:** Two-step moderate-hard new-meaning candidate supported by a CC BY technical review and independent series.

#### postop-infected-collection-drain - revised

Before: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-infected-collection-drain.v1`; attempt: `question.topic.pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia.postop-infected-collection-drain.v2`; exact after SHA-256 `64b7c957c9cc24c0f515f84df703848d000e65002d3278eeee69558ee45f4bcd`.

- **clarity:** Replaced promised existing-tract repositioning with image-guided catheter drainage, allowing placement or exchange as IR determines.
- **cues:** Removed explicit tip-outside-cavity and feasible-route conclusions. A compact CT table shows side-hole compartment, separate collection and intervening anatomy.
- **fairness:** The reader infers ineffective compartment drainage and then chooses the initial intervention level. Stability, absence of generalized peritonitis and access anatomy remain for fairness. Operative washout is credible; no technically guaranteed catheter maneuver is claimed.
- **suggestions:** Antibiotics with reassessment, image-guided source control and operative source control are same-stage plans. The rubric identifies when surgery becomes appropriate, without inventing an EUS-access rule or antibiotic regimen.
- **outcome:** Two-step moderate-hard candidate using the existing directly verified postoperative review; single-source limitation remains explicit.

### Evidence, rights and timing

The [owned source ledger](sources-question-topic-pancreas-chronic-cysts-neoplasia-20261111.json) preserves its original records and adds `reviewResponse`: all 16 complete source records, 45 atomic claims, bidirectional source/claim/question mappings and statement mappings for the eight PASS versions and twelve revision attempts. New administration facts use the government-hosted approved PANCREAZE label; functional regionalization uses Zhao et al. (2020, CC BY 4.0) plus Halmi et al. (2024, CC BY); metal-stent recurrent-obstruction reasoning uses Lyu et al. (2023, CC BY 4.0) plus the existing consensus. Medical authority and reuse permission are separate in every source record. The regulatory manufacturer text is not presumed public domain. No source text, table, figure, algorithm or exact study effect is copied.

Postoperative source control retains its one-direct-review limitation. No new peritoneal-cytology, exact grade cutoff, insulin-response ratio, dose amount, bilirubin threshold or drug regimen is keyed. New quantitative patient observations are constructed values rather than prevalence or invented clinical cutoffs. Inaccessible/challenged or unsuitable-license candidates are recorded as excluded and support no new claim. The original withheld policy points remain unscored.

Every diagnostic/procedure choice has exact identity/label timing metadata using existing placeholder profiles. Source links use `_blank`, `noopener noreferrer` and `no-referrer`. No fixed waits are embedded in prose. All orders are planning or outside-record review with null executable services/result gates; the manager owns any eventual registry admission.

### Minimal context and independent reasoning checks

- **chronic-failed-stenting:** Retain the named age/sex profile, chronic-pancreatitis diagnosis and outside-record consultation. The exact update already supplies nutritional response, prior endotherapy, current duct anatomy and operative fitness. The mistimed-enzyme scored predecessor is omitted. Its prescription details and answer are not needed to interpret the supplied later nutritional response.
- **functional-net-enucleation:** Retain the established functional syndrome, negative hereditary evaluation, CT staging and operative fitness. The exact update supplies lesion size, superficial position, duct separation and local staging. The non-PASS EUS-selection predecessor is omitted. The completed EUS result is supplied directly by the preserved update; no learner-selected investigation is assumed.
- **ipmn-high-risk-plan:** Retain the incidental cyst and original symptom/history negatives. The exact MRI update provides communication, measured duct/nodule findings, distant staging and operative fitness. The non-PASS initial-modality predecessor and its inadequate urogram acquisition are omitted. The returned MRI is an existing outside report rather than a consequence of a scored answer.
- **mcn-large-symptomatic:** Identify A and B and retain their observed chronology so the exact update's A, B and subsequent studies have clear referents. Persistent fullness, compression, current size, sampling and fitness remain in the unmodified update. The non-PASS referral-disposition node and its answer are omitted. The outside record supplies completed MRI/EUS; no decision about MRI versus EUS is scored or implied.
- **net-growth-duct-proximity:** Introduce the original small body NET and surveillance phase so the exact later-growth update has its baseline. The update independently supplies the old sample, new duct effect, current staging and fitness. The non-PASS initial surveillance decision, unexplained unchanged duct statement and follow-up permission are omitted. Surveillance is a recorded historical course, not an additional scored node.
- **postop-transient-drain-bleed:** Establish the pancreatic operation, outside readmission, collection and drain so later in the same admission and the collection have explicit referents. The exact update supplies the bleeding, hemoglobin change and current hospital circulation. Both earlier scored hospital decisions are omitted. The recorded postoperative collection and operative drain are background from the same constructed source record; no new drainage result or source-control procedure is asserted.
- **postop-vomiting-inflammation:** Retain only the operation and retrospective hospital-record frame. The exact first-node update already states the symptoms, inflammatory trajectory, drain change and contemporaneous stability. The non-PASS source-control companion and the later bleeding decision are omitted. No future collection finding, catheter position or complication diagnosis is included in this presentation.

The bleeding case introduces the prior admission, collection and drain so that the unchanged phrase about a later event in the same admission has a referent. It adds no postoperative interval or vascular diagnosis. The MCN case identifies A and B and their existing chronology; it does not disclose a mucinous diagnosis or choose a treatment. The functional-NET feedback retains its optional prior-case comparison verbatim because the manager requires exact PASS wording; the operation can be selected from this case's own presentation and update. These details are called out for the targeted reviewer.

      "learningSummary": "A was present before the first attack; B appeared afterward. That does not prove A is neoplastic, but it prevents attributing A's origin to this attack. Redirect the named therapeutic referral to cyst characterization. EUS is reasonable for this enlarged symptomatic cyst; MRI/MRCP can also contribute, and this question does not rank those two studies against each other. The combined location, lack of duct communication and mucinous fluid assessment favor presumed MCN rather than establish its histology. A's size and persistent gastric compression support resection evaluation. CEA does not diagnose invasive cancer, and scant bland cells do not establish safety. Repeat sampling need not delay referral when the decision already rests on size and symptoms."

      "learningSummary": "Vomiting after pancreatic surgery should not be assigned to isolated delayed emptying while systemic inflammation and changing drain behavior suggest a secondary complication. CT is the appropriate offered initial assessment of the current abdomen. Duct mapping or functional testing addresses different remaining questions. The catheter does not drain the cavity shown on CT. Antibiotics need effective source control, and this stable record supports image-guided repositioning rather than immediate reoperation. A separate duct-directed treatment would require its own anatomic assessment; it is not a substitute for draining the current infected cavity. Cessation does not make this episode reassuring. Postoperative pancreatic leakage can be associated with vascular erosion and later major hemorrhage. In the currently stable record, urgent CT angiography can identify a source for endovascular treatment. This is a review of hospital-level care; the clinic does not execute it."
    },
